title: Agent Instruction Placement And Effectiveness Probe

blocks.text: C4 Provider Runtime owns only how an assignment-created `Assignment.agent_instruction` snapshot is delivered to each provider surface. It does not own the client-authored instruction text, assignment-time snapshot decision, or 1000-character limit.

The matrix is implemented by `RuntimeInstructionStrategies()` and consumed by `ApplyRuntimeInstructionContract`. Public CI verifies deterministic placement, metadata, idempotent section composition, and provider-neutral effectiveness probe shape without executing external provider CLIs.

Provider-specific effectiveness means the real provider obeys the delivered instruction after it is placed on that provider's chosen surface. It is verified by `BuildInstructionEffectivenessProbe` and `ValidateInstructionEffectivenessOutput`; real provider execution remains opt-in integration evidence.

RIID-5817: Concrete implementation requests require actual work and verification. Codex user input starts with the task while reusable instructions use native developerInstructions. Cursor preserves separately supplied system instructions through an inline fallback. See docs/30-architecture/agent-task-execution.md for bounded host verification and correction.

RIID-5860: User-facing progress must describe the actual current or completed action for this task in the user’s language. Preserve the code meanings on every instruction surface: 1001 thinking, 1101 tool collecting, 1102 collection completed count, 1103 tool running, and 1104 tool completed. Existing codes 1101/1103 carry one short sentence in args.description; 1104 carries one short sentence in args.summary. Labels stay short state-neutral nouns. Target approximately 120 characters for the sentence; do not emit raw commands, code, internal function or tool names, debug logs, prompt dumps, secrets, or long answer drafts.

Emit progress only when meaningful work changes, not as repeated filler or a fixed periodic phrase. Report only observed work and verified completion; never invent a tool result, success, waiting reason, or another task being busy. Code 1001 is reserved for an initial state when no concrete progress can yet be reported. The same rules apply to injected provider instructions and native-config hard rules; existing message codes, argument schema, parsing, execution, partial answers, and final results stay unchanged. Deterministic tests prove instruction delivery and constraints, not real-provider compliance.
